title: Recursive choice tree for permutations of distinct elements
summary: Starting from an empty prefix, choose one unused element from [1, 2, 3] in each round and append it to state, producing 6 permutations after three rounds.
context: The candidate array is choices = [1, 2, 3], whose three elements are distinct and may each be used only once per permutation. The root node is drawn as three blank slots representing the empty prefix [] before any element is chosen; the blank slots themselves are not element values.
description: The figure expands all recursive branches simultaneously; in actual backtracking execution, after copying and saving state at a leaf node, the code pops the last element and marks it unselected again before trying sibling branches.
The choice tree has four levels, from the empty prefix at level 0 to the leaf nodes at level 3. The two tables below look up available next choices by prefix and list all six permutations by index.

frames.title: Recursive choice tree for permutations of distinct elements
frames.explanation: Across the first, second, and third rounds, each node has 3, 2, and 1 available elements respectively, generating 3 × 2 × 1 = 6 leaf nodes corresponding to all 6 permutations of [1, 2, 3].
